facts.fact: The Adwave article states that when an email lands in spam, its open rate can plummet by as much as 90%.
facts.quote: When an email lands in spam, its open rate can plummet by as much as **90%**.

facts.fact: The Adwave article states that a healthy email campaign might reach an average open rate of 43.46%.
facts.quote: A healthy campaign might hit a **43.46%** average open rate

facts.fact: The Adwave article states that an email stuck in a junk folder often struggles to reach even a 5% open rate.
facts.quote: one stuck in a junk folder often struggles to reach even **5%**.

facts.fact: The Adwave article states that personalizing a subject line can lift open rates by 26%.
facts.quote: Personalizing a subject line can lift open rates by a whopping **26%**.

facts.fact: 73% of users check email on their phones, according to the page.
facts.quote: With **73% of users** checking email on their phones, a huge wall of text is an instant "delete."

facts.fact: Properly segmented email lists reduced unsubscribe rates from a 0.22% average to almost zero, according to Adwave's experience.
facts.quote: We've seen properly segmented lists slash unsubscribe rates from a painful **0.22%** average down to almost zero.

facts.fact: Adwave recommends targeting subscribers who have not opened an email in 90 days as a re-engagement segment.
facts.quote: those who haven't opened an email in **90 days**

facts.fact: HubSpot research shows well-delivered e-commerce emails can see average conversion rates of 2.68%.
facts.quote: research from HubSpot](https://www.hubspot.com/marketing-statistics) shows that well-delivered e-commerce emails can see average conversion rates of **2.68%**.

facts.fact: The page recommends keeping email paragraphs to one to three sentences.
facts.quote: One to three sentences is the sweet spot.

facts.fact: The page states that DMARC tells ISPs what to do with emails that fail SPF or DKIM checks, such as marking them as spam or rejecting them.
facts.quote: It tells ISPs what to do with emails that fail the SPF or DKIM checks, like marking them as spam or rejecting them completely.

facts.fact: The page estimates that the email world will have about 4.6 billion users by 2026.
facts.quote: By 2026, the email world will be home to an estimated **4.6 billion** users

facts.fact: The page states that emails that make it through spam filters see a B2C conversion rate of 2.8%.
facts.quote: emails that make it through see B2C conversion rates of **2.8%**, which consistently leaves paid social in the dust.
